News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 17:57:17 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category></category><title>Will Spain's far right replace Europe's left-wing stalwart?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261126-will-spain-s-far-right-replace-europe-s-left-wing-stalwart</link><description>
Some 39 million Spaniards will head to the ballot this Sunday to vote in early general elections. Latest polls put the conservative Popular Party ahead of incumbent PM Pedro Sanchez’s Socialists. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/13ac116c-e9b8-11f1-b82e-77d069279b82/w:1024/p:16x9/Thumb-Spain-01.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/13ac116c-e9b8-11f1-b82e-77d069279b82/w:1024/p:16x9/Thumb-Spain-01.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">34c2cfb2-e9b8-11f1-bd33-01df7f3018c8</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 16:51:54 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Across Africa</category><title>ACROSS AFRICA:  Tunisian Photographer's Family Focus</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/across-africa-tunisian-photographer-s-family-focus-1</link><description>
Stories from the continent with Georja Calvin-Smith. This week, health workers struggling to keep pace with DR Congo's Ebola outbreak say they feel abandoned and unsupported. Also, the World Cup was about more than winning... for some fans, at least. Tunisia's performance may not have been all that its supporters had hoped, but sports photographer Hosni Manoubi is far from negative about a family tradition of documenting his country's international sports showings. [Archive Episode, June 2026]
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d42e595e-e9b3-11f1-9008-1991d4929b54/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-ebcee408.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d42e595e-e9b3-11f1-9008-1991d4929b54/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-ebcee408.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0134df40-70a1-11f1-a2d1-bbc19ff962e2</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 16:19:12 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Georja CALVIN-SMITH</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>In California, exceptional tides and nearly 9m-high waves batter the coast</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261126-in-california-exceptional-tides-and-nearly-9m-high-waves-batter-the-coast</link><description>
USA: Powerful waves and king tides destroyed part of a pier in Pacifica, south of San Francisco, on Wednesday. In Marin County, authorities issued a temporary evacuation order and urged people to stay away from the beach. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3da49d80-e9af-11f1-b62c-1991d4929b54/w:1024/p:16x9/CALIFORNIA-Minia.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3da49d80-e9af-11f1-b62c-1991d4929b54/w:1024/p:16x9/CALIFORNIA-Minia.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6775884a-e9af-11f1-9f80-5fc06f4e7cce</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 16:01:44 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Spanish economist de Cos to succeed Lagarde as head of ECB</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261126-spanish-economist-de-cos-succeed-lagarde-head-ecb</link><description>
Spanish monetary economist Pablo Hernandez de Cos on Thursday was set to replace France's Christine Lagarde as the new head of the European Central Bank (ECB). His nomination comes as the Europe's most powerful financial institution grapples with an Iran war-driven resurgence in inflation and a cost of living crisis.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8782840e-e9a4-11f1-a5e6-f9cf020caef6/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25290616236227.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8782840e-e9a4-11f1-a5e6-f9cf020caef6/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25290616236227.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c00b4f90-e9a9-11f1-b052-5576e34b99b1</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 15:55:45 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8782840e-e9a4-11f1-a5e6-f9cf020caef6/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25290616236227.jpg">© Jose Luis Magana, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>arts24</category><title>Lost homes, stolen freedom: National Book Award winners on exile and imprisonment</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/arts24/20261126-lost-homes-stolen-freedom-national-book-award-winners-on-exile-and-imprisonment</link><description>
Two books about losing everything have just won America's most prestigious literary honours. Hannah Lillith Assadi took the National Book Award for fiction for "Paradiso 17", a novel inspired by her late father, who was driven from Palestine in 1948 during the Nakba. Abdelrahman ElGendy won the non-fiction prize for "Huna", his memoir of six years as a political prisoner in Egypt, arrested at 17 alongside his father. ElGendy couldn't be in New York to collect his award: his visa was denied.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/faf78374-e9a6-11f1-a42f-81bc2b1dcd65/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-5c1d3af7.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/faf78374-e9a6-11f1-a42f-81bc2b1dcd65/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-5c1d3af7.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">333234c4-e9a6-11f1-8b14-3fb642790777</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 15:41:38 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Eve JACKSON</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

]]> <![CDATA[ Venus shines at its brightest in the predawn sky this week. Here's where to look ]]> Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know.

As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky.

Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane.

When is Venus at its most dazzling?

Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky. Stargazers in the U.S. could get an incredible view of Venus in the predawn hours of the coming week, as the planet climbs into the southeastern sky ahead of the rising sun, with Mercury clinging close to the horizon below.

Celestron Nexstar 4SE

This is a fantastic go-to telescope with a 4-inch aperture and can help you quickly find a steady view of the moon. For a closer look at craters and the terminator, make sure to grab a 9mm or 12mm eyepiece and get stronger magnification.

_

Celestron Nexstar 4SE review

The bright star Spica will glow less than five degrees away from Venus before dawn on Nov. 27 — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length against the night sky.

Spica is a double system of two stars that orbit one another once every four days. Its stars are separated by just approximately 11 million miles (less than 18 million kilometers), making them far too close to split visually with even the most powerful amateur equipment. However, the system still makes for a dazzling target, appearing as a magnificent blue-white star when viewed through the eyepiece of a 4-inch telescope.

Check that the sun is safely below the horizon before turning your telescope on Venus to observe a crescent of light playing across the planet's dense atmosphere. What is it?

Roughly 6,800 light-years from Earth and nestled in the Centaurus constellation, this piece of the supernova remnant SNR G295.5+09.7 has earned the nickname the Betta Fish Nebula for its floaty, fishy shape.

This almost ghostly whirl of gas and dust was created when a star much more massive than our sun exploded, blasting its outer layers of material outward in the process. Over time, the remnants of this supernova eruption stretched outward into space, dispersing and colliding with surrounding gas. The explosive remnants mixing with gas in the interstellar medium created this glowing, blue cloud.

And while researchers this past January revealed the initial result of this six-year survey, scientists continue to explore the possibilities of dark energy with DECam alongside instruments like the recently-launched Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

However, while the survey has lofty goals with its DECam data, the camera can also capture beautiful imagery like this cerulean wisp thousands of light-years away.

]]> <![CDATA[ Thanksgiving night sky 2026 — What to look for after dinner tonight ]]> If your household is like most American families, then on Thursday you likely will all be sitting down with family and friends for a traditional Thanksgiving turkey dinner during the mid-to-late afternoon hours.

Then as darkness falls, some will probably migrate into the living room to catch some football or other holiday fare on television. But if you have a large gathering of family and friends at your home — and if your skies are mainly clear — why not invite everyone outside to gaze at the evening sky?

If you have binoculars, or better yet, a telescope, you just might end up turning this into a memorable family tradition of its own.

First, the "Lord of the Rings" . . .

If I may paraphrase the mysterious voice from the 1989 movie, "Field of Dreams": "If you set up your telescope, they will come." And you'll get a big kick out of your Turkey Day guests uttering all the "oohs" and "ahs" or exclamations of "Wow!" with just one peek through the eyepiece.

As darkness falls, Saturn will glow at first magnitude, shining with a sedate, yellow-white light and appearing noticeably brighter than the star Fomalhaut, about 40 degrees (the equivalent of four fist-widths) to its lower right.

Its famous ring system is now tilted only about six degrees toward Earth but may be visible with steadied (or image-stabilized) high-power binoculars or through the eyepiece of a telescope magnifying over 30-power. The rings will seem to glow with an inner light and for those who have never had the pleasure of seeing them for themselves, that first view always elicits astonishment; kids especially most often will say: "Awesome!" or "No way!" I've even had people accuse me of using a slide of Saturn, to which I, of course, reply with, "No . . . that's the real thing."

. . . and later, the moon

Then, along about 6:25 p.m. local time, the waning gibbous moon, 2½ days past full phase and 91% illuminated, will begin to emerge from beyond the east-northeast horizon. Give it another hour and it will stand about 10 degrees above the horizon — equal to the width of your clenched fist held at arm's length. By then, the moon will be in a better position for evening study.

Even in binoculars, the moon is a striking sight to see. It's such a special object because it doesn't matter whether you live in a rural area or in the middle of a brightly lit city, for the moon can always be readily observed. It always looks spectacular whether you're using binoculars or a telescope. It never looks precisely the same no matter how often you view it and can be observed even on hazy or partially cloud-covered nights.

Pay particular attention to the line of darkness — called the terminator — features near that border stand out in bold relief; the shadows become stronger and details are more easily seen. Take note on this night of the circular dark area, bisected by the terminator: Mare Crisium — the "Sea of Crises." Immediately bordering above it is a 50-mile (80 km)-wide ring of very rugged mountains, rising as high as 14,400 feet (4,389 meters), which now resembles a huge crater partially in shadow when the sun is low.

A bonus: A view of the International Space Station

Probably the one object that your Thanksgiving guests will want to see is the biggest and brightest of all the man-made objects orbiting the Earth: the International Space Station (ISS). Except for those living across the southern US, for most everywhere else, the ISS will be making visible passes on Thanksgiving evening.


Circling the Earth at an average altitude of 260 miles (420 km) and at a speed of 17,500 mph (28,200 kph), it can appear to move as fast as a high-flying jet airliner, sometimes taking as much as six or seven minutes to cross the sky. It can easily be confused with aircraft lights. Nominally, it appears white with a slight yellow tinge and at its very brightest it can sometimes appear to shine as bright as magnitude -5.6, which is twice as bright as the planet Venus!

So, what is the viewing schedule on Thanksgiving for your hometown? You can easily find out by visiting one of three popular websites:

Spot the Station

This site will tell you when and where to sight the ISS. All you need do is type in your city or town, then click on the map pinpoint to get all the details. You can even sign up to get email or text alerts when the space station is flying over.

Chris Peat's Heavens Above

This site will not only provide you with sighting information for the ISS, but also for many other satellites as well. You must first register and then you can input your location to generate a sighting schedule.

Live Real-Time Satellite Tracking

Like Heavens Above, you can get sighting information for the ISS and other satellites. Once you log on this site will automatically provide details based on your IP address ... or you can set a "custom" location.

Here at Space.com, we like to wish a very happy and safe Thanksgiving to all, and of course, clear skies!

]]> <![CDATA[ Space plants with hot sauce: What ISS astronauts will be eating on Thanksgiving (video) ]]>

The astronauts on the International Space Station will celebrate Thanksgiving with some nontraditional fare.

Well, NASA astronaut Anil Menon will, anyway. In a video the agency released on Monday (Nov. 23), Menon showed off some of the plants he and his crewmates are growing in orbit and told us what's in store for the greens.

"We need plants to survive as we set up our moon base, and as we go to Mars, we're going to have to grow our own nutrition. So that's what we're doing this Thanksgiving," Menon said in the 2.5-minute video.

"I plan on using this [plant] with a tortilla and some pasta and some hot sauce to make my Thanksgiving meal," added Menon, who was wearing a chef's toque for the occasion. "And I'm grateful for you and for my family at home."

He passed the microphone to fellow NASA astronaut Luke Delaney, who didn't talk about food but expressed gratitude to his family, crewmates and support network on Earth.

Next up was NASA's Jessica Watkins, who gave us a rundown of the broader Thanksgiving menu in space.

"Some of what we'll be eating here — we've got some roasted turkey, some mac and cheese, some mashed potatoes, and some candied yams," Watkins said, showing off the small bags containing each of those comestibles. "So, we should be in good shape."

The Canadian Space Agency's (CSA) Joshua Kutryk spoke next. He said he'll eat rice and the space-grown plants, which he'll consume raw "because it reminds me of Earth, which I miss."

All four of the astronauts then wished us a happy Thanksgiving and did some zero-g flips and rolls, sending the space plants on a bit of a ride.

Delaney, Kutryk and Watkins are members of SpaceX's Crew-13 mission, which arrived at the International Space Station (ISS) on Oct. 1. There's a fourth Crew-13 astronaut as well — Sergey Teteryatnikov, of the Russian space agency Roscosmos.

That quartet shares the ISS with Menon and cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anna Kikina, who arrived in July aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft.

Astronauts tend to get major holidays off on the ISS, and to celebrate them together. Doing so reinforces the already-strong bonds the crewmates share and helps them deal with the pain of being away from friends and family, which can be especially acute on holidays like Thanksgiving and Christmas.

Kutryk is likely feeling especially emotional these days. On Tuesday, the CSA announced that Kutryk's wife had given birth to the couple's third child, a daughter.

"Even with the distance between us, we feel incredibly connected as we welcome our new little star into our lives," the couple said in a statement shared by the CSA. "We are very proud of our growing family and are looking forward to getting our little crew of five all reunited."

 <description>Městský soud v Praze začal ve čtvrtek projednávat žalobu, kterou podalo Hnutí Duha na ministra zahraničí Petra Macinku.       <title>Česko bojuje se sněhem. Kolabuje veřejná doprava, hlášené jsou stovky nehod</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/cesko-snih-pocasi-silnice-predpoved.A261126_071836_domaci_pluh#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Dopravu v Česku od rána komplikuje sníh, policie řeší kromě řady nehod také uvázlé kamiony. Problémy se objevují také ve veřejné dopravě, zejména autobusy na některých místech Vysočiny či Jihomoravského kraje nevyjíždějí. Zásadní zlepšení se neočekává ani v následujících hodinách. Meteorologové očekávají, že sněžení postupně zasáhne většinu území, na některých místech připadnout až 15 centimetrů.</description>

Vyplývá to z dlouhodobého výzkumu Psychologického ústavu Akademie věd ČR a agentury Median, podle kterého velmi nebo spíše důvěřuje veřejnoprávním médiím 48 procent respondentů.</description></item><item><title>Od šelem až do pralesa: Zoo a botanickou propojí v sobotu zážitková stezka</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906741-od-selem-az-do-pralesa-zoologickou-a-botanickou-zahradu-propoji-v-sobotu-stezka.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906741-od-selem-az-do-pralesa-zoologickou-a-botanickou-zahradu-propoji-v-sobotu-stezka.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:20:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>V sobotu 28. listopadu čeká rodiny s dětmi v Liberci netradiční dobrodružství. Zážitková stezka plná úkolů propojí zdejší zoologickou a botanickou zahradu. Výprava odstartuje mezi zvířaty v zoo, povede lesíkem a vyvrcholí v tropických sklenících botanické zahrady.</description></item><item><title>V republice kolem nuly, v Liberci mráz. Výstraha na sníh v kraji tentokrát neplatí</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906738-v-republice-kolem-nuly-v-liberci-mraz-vystraha-na-snih-v-kraji-tentokrat-neplati.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906738-v-republice-kolem-nuly-v-liberci-mraz-vystraha-na-snih-v-kraji-tentokrat-neplati.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 07:51:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Zatímco jinde v republice byly noční teploty jen kolem nuly, v Libereckém kraji klesly hluboko pod bod mrazu. V Liberci bylo k ránu až -10 stupňů Celsia a na Jizerce dokonce teplota klesla na -15 stupňů. Meteorologická výstraha před silným sněžením se Libereckého kraje tentokrát netýká.</description></item><item><title>Soud požádal Senát o vydání Půty k trestnímu stíhání</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/906734-soud-pozadal-senat-o-vydani-puty-k-trestnimu-stihani.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/906734-soud-pozadal-senat-o-vydani-puty-k-trestnimu-stihani.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 06:26:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Vrchní soud v Praze požádal Senát o vydání senátora a libereckého hejtmana Martina Půty (Starostové pro Liberecký kraj) k trestnímu stíhání. Půta to uvedl na síti X. Doplnil, že již před druhým kolem senátních voleb, ve kterých byl zvolen, avizoval, že bude s vydáním souhlasit.</description></item><item><title>Domácností s dětmi v EU ubývá. Česko je nad průměrem, porodnost ale padá</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906454-domacnosti-s-detmi-v-eu-ubyva-cesko-je-nad-prumerem-porodnost-ale-pada.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906454-domacnosti-s-detmi-v-eu-ubyva-cesko-je-nad-prumerem-porodnost-ale-pada.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 19:56:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Jiří Komárek</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Domácností s dětmi v Evropské unii dlouhodobě ubývá. Podle dat, která Eurostat zveřejnil 20. listopadu, v roce 2025 nežily děti mladší 18 let v 76,6 % evropských domácností. Podíl domácností s dětmi klesá bez přerušení: v roce 2010 činil 26,9 %, loňského roku už pouze 23,3 %.</description></item><item><title>Liberecký kraj bude sčítat návštěvníky Ještědu, cílem je udržitelný turismus</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906660-liberecky-kraj-bude-scitat-navstevniky-jestedu-cilem-je-udrzitelny.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906660-liberecky-kraj-bude-scitat-navstevniky-jestedu-cilem-je-udrzitelny.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 18:20:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Liberecký kraj bude sčítat návštěvníky Ještědu. Projekt souvisí s plány kraje na zapsání horského hotelu a vysílače na jeho vrcholu na Seznam světového dědictví UNESCO. Cílem je udržitelný turismus, který nebude poškozovat památkově chráněnou budovu ani její okolí.</description></item></channel></rss>

]]> Ezagutu Lužice aneb Poznejte Lužici https://www.vybezek.eu/297720-ezagutu-luzice-aneb-poznejte-luzici/ Mon, 23 Nov 2026 18:23:04 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=297720 Literárně naučné miniturné po Čechách lužickosrbské spisovatelky Róži Domašcyny, básníka a překladatele Milana Hrabala a hudebníka Vojtěcha Kouby.

Ve dnech 3. a 4. listopadu 2026 proběhly dva večery věnované lužickosrbské literatuře a kultuře pod názvem Ezagutu Lužice (Poznejte Lužici), které pořádaly, ruku v ruce, nakladatelství Euskaldun a Společnost přátel Lužice. Nejednalo se o první takovou spolupráci, ale o vyvrcholení celého cyklu pořadů věnovaným menším jazykovým skupinám bez vlastní státnosti, které jsou nějakým způsobem svázány s českými zeměmi. První večer proběhl v Plzni v univerzitní kavárně Družba a následující den se přesunul takříkajíc na domácí hřiště do pražského Lužického semináře.

Hlavními hvězdami večerů byly Róža Domašcyna, jedna z nejvýznamnějších lužickosrbských autorek a Milan Hrabal, básník, překladatel, přítel a propagátor Lužice. O hudební doprovod se postaral Vojtěch Kouba, který představil publiku lužický folklór, ale zároveň i vlastní tvorbu.

Na první večer dorazilo asi čtyřicet zvídavých Plzeňanů, pro které bylo setkání s literaturou a historií nejmenšího západoslovanského národa iniciačním zážitkem. Milan Hrabal se ukázal, jako výborný průvodce lužicko-srbskými reáliemi i historií. Navíc bavil publikum tím, jak se postupně přiznával k různým překladatelským přehmatům. Poezie Róži Domašcyny a písně Vojtěcha Kouby vykouzlily čarovnou atmosféru jak v plzeňské studentské kavárně, tak pod barokní klenbou Lužického semináře.

Sychravé počasí za okny kontrastovalo s vřelou a neformální atmosférou obou večerů. U srdce zahřály i reakce návštěvníků. Etablovaný plzeňský básník Jan Sojka poklekl před organizátory večera na kolena, líbal jim ruce a děkoval za krásný večer. Herpetolog Ondřej Škach zase prohlásil, že nelituje toho, že vyměnil oslavu úspěšného odchovu zmije pavoučí v plzeňské ZOO, za lužickosrbský večer, neboť o zmijích ví všechno, ale o Lužici nevěděl doposud nic. Filolog Mikuláš Liptovský se nechal výkonem účinkujících dokonce strhnout ke slibu, že se na stará kolena pustí do studia sorabistiky. Studenty pražských uměleckých škol zase okouzlil Milan Hrabal natolik, že se zajímali o to, kdy bude mít v Lužickém semináři příští seminář o Lužici. Není divu, že se návštěvníci nechali vtáhnout do průběhu večera. Byl totiž úplně jiný, než obvykle literární večery bývají. Domašcyna s Hrabalem jsou na sebe mentálně navázaní a je na jejich vystoupení znát, že jsou sehraná dvojice. Kouba je pak skvěle doplňuje svými písněmi. Většina diváků slyšela asi poprvé dylanovku v lužické srbštině.  O pozitivních pocitech publika svědčí i ovace ve stoje, které následovaly po pražském večeru.

V době, kdy některé vlády vedou kulturní války proti vlastním občanům, tito se jim staví literaturou a radostí, kterou přináší umění slova. Je hezké vidět, když se lidé sejdou, aby vyslechli hlas malého národa a tím se o něco víc přiblížili ke břehům ostrova zapomenutých.

Martin Holý , Euskaldun
